learn.title: Cosine and sine as coordinates
learn.body: The unit circle has radius 1 and sits at the origin. Turn by an angle $\theta$ from the positive $x$-axis and you land on a point. Its coordinates are $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$. Tangent is $\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.

learn.title: Key values
learn.body: At $0^\circ$ the point is $(1,0)$. At $30^\circ$ it is $\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2},\frac12\right)$. At $45^\circ$ it is $\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2},\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)$. At $60^\circ$ it is $\left(\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)$. At $90^\circ$ it is $(0,1)$.

learn.title: Signs by quadrant
learn.body: In quadrant I both coordinates are positive. In II, $\cos$ is negative. In III both are negative. In IV, $\sin$ is negative. Because the point is on the circle, $\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$.

learn.title: Find $\sin 150^\circ$
steps: $150^\circ$ is in quadrant II, $30^\circ$ from the negative $x$-axis
$\sin$ is positive in quadrant II, so $\sin150^\circ=\frac12$

questions.explanation: At angle 0 the point is $(1,0)$, and cosine is the $x$-coordinate.
Reference angle $60^\circ$, and $\cos$ is negative in quadrant II.

questions.prompt: An angle in quadrant I has $\cos\theta=\frac35$. What is $\sin\theta$? Give a decimal.
questions.explanation: $\sin^2\theta=1-\frac{9}{25}=\frac{16}{25}$, and sine is positive in quadrant I, so $\frac45=0.8$.

questions.prompt: Match each angle to its sine.
questions.explanation: Sine is the height of the point. It rises from 0 to 1 over the first quadrant.
